body:
### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.statusline

### Question

I accidentally opened a PR for this as a proposed fix before I was able to test it locally, but for a little bit of context-ish, the PR is https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/pull/1555

I don't really know if I'd consider this an issue, but more of a user error right now.

Anywho, the root issue is that the `section_filename` will return the full path, because I always use my terminal full-screen and thus the truncate logic never triggers.

So I see this:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/67ee31d7-fbb5-4bfe-a118-0aa5b6aac13b)

When I would prefer seeing this even in full screen:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e2e57505-ef57-486e-93d0-102450bbe30a)

My current config for statusline looks like this:

```lua
local MiniStatusline = require("mini.statusline")

local statusline_config = function()
        local mode, mode_hl = MiniStatusline.section_mode({ trunc_width = 120 })
        local git = MiniStatusline.section_git({ trunc_width = 40 })
        local diff = MiniStatusline.section_diff({ trunc_width = 75 })
        local diagnostics = MiniStatusline.section_diagnostics({ trunc_width = 75 })
        local lsp = MiniStatusline.section_lsp({ trunc_width = 75 })
        local filename = MiniStatusline.section_filename({ trunc_width = 1 })
        local fileinfo = MiniStatusline.section_fileinfo({ trunc_width = 120 })
        local location = MiniStatusline.section_location({ trunc_width = 1 })
        local search = MiniStatusline.section_searchcount({ trunc_width = 75 })

        return MiniStatusline.combine_groups({
                { hl = mode_hl,                  strings = { mode } },
                {
                        hl = "MiniStatuslineDevinfo",
                        strings = { git, diff, lsp },
                },
                "%<", -- Mark general truncate point
                { hl = "MiniStatuslineFilename", strings = { filename } },
                "%=", -- End left alignment
                -- { hl = "MiniStatuslineFileinfo", strings = { fileinfo } },
                { hl = mode_hl, strings = { search, location } },
        })
end

MiniStatusline.setup({
        content = { active = statusline_config },
})
```

Unless I'm missing something, but whether `trunc_width` is 1 (as it is now) or a big number, it's the same result.

comment_data.body:
> Unless I'm missing something, but whether `trunc_width` is 1 (as it is now) or a big number, it's the same result.

With the code provided, having something like `local filename = MiniStatusline.section_filename({ trunc_width = 9999 })` (use short form if width is less than 9999, i.e. realistically always) makes it always show in the short form for me. A short form uses `%f` item from `:h 'statusline'` which is transformed into "Path to the file in the buffer, as typed or relative to current directory". So in order for file name to be relative to the project's root (or something else you'd expect it be relative to), make sure that Neovim's current working directory is set to it. You can check it via `:pwd` and change via `:cd` (or navigating inside it in the terminal before starting Neovim).

If you don't want this adjustable behavior from neither `section_fileinfo()` or `section_location()`, you can use their return value directly without calling the sections. With something like this:

```lua
local statusline_config = function()
  local mode, mode_hl = MiniStatusline.section_mode({ trunc_width = 120 })
  local git = MiniStatusline.section_git({ trunc_width = 40 })
  local diff = MiniStatusline.section_diff({ trunc_width = 75 })
  local lsp = MiniStatusline.section_lsp({ trunc_width = 75 })
  local filename = vim.bo.buftype == 'terminal' and '%t' or '%f%m%r'
  local fileinfo = MiniStatusline.section_fileinfo({ trunc_width = 120 })
  local location = '%l│%2v'
  local search = MiniStatusline.section_searchcount({ trunc_width = 75 })

  return MiniStatusline.combine_groups({
    { hl = mode_hl, strings = { mode } },
    { hl = 'MiniStatuslineDevinfo', strings = { git, diff, lsp } },
    '%<', -- Mark general truncate point
    { hl = 'MiniStatuslineFilename', strings = { filename } },
    '%=', -- End left alignment
    -- { hl = "MiniStatuslineFileinfo", strings = { fileinfo } },
    { hl = mode_hl, strings = { search, location } },
  })
end

require('mini.statusline').setup({
  content = { active = statusline_config },
})
```

For which statusline items to use, see `:h 'statusline'` or ['mini.statusline' source code directly](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/87fc38a8a2b8d498cecb021d057a38ea2e9f5a79/lua/mini/statusline.lua#L373-L385).
